key_insight: TRACE is a single energy-conserving interatomic potential architecture that combines atomic cluster expansion with local multihead cross-attention to model complex many-body chemistry without passing learned state between atoms.
engineering_relevance: It offers a scalable, physically grounded route to simulate phase behavior, liquid structure, and reactive pathways across multiple materials systems on modest hardware.
method: Uses O(3)-equivariant atomic cluster expansion density correlations as the per-atom state.
Applies local multihead cross-attention to fixed tensorial neighbor features derived from species and geometry.
Trains one unified potential and validates it with enhanced/umbrella sampling for difficult transformations and barriers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement with experiment and high-level theory across cesium lead iodide polymorph ordering and transition temperature, water O–O structure, and methyl migration activation free energy.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on selected benchmark systems, so broader transferability and robustness to new chemistries or larger-scale simulations still need careful validation.
